title: Saints Peter and Paul (29 June)
hookLine: the fisherman and the tentmaker, the two pillars of Rome

cards: Two giant stone statues stand guard in front of Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome. On one side, Peter, holding keys. On the other, Paul, holding a sword.
The Church gives them one feast together, on the twenty-ninth of June, which is a little funny, because they didn't always get along. One was a fisherman from Galilee.
The other was an educated Pharisee from a city in what is now southern Turkey who made tents for a living. And once, in front of everyone, one of them told the other he was wrong.

teach.h: PETROS: THE ROCK, AND THE KEYS.
teach.b: Peter first. Simon, son of John, a fisherman, renamed by Jesus, in the Douay-Rheims: "thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church." Petros, rock.
The keys in his statue come from the next line, the keys of the kingdom. Catholics see in Peter the first of the popes, the bishop of Rome.
He's also the one who sank in the water, who denied Jesus three times, and who was forgiven on a beach. Then Paul.
Saul of Tarsus, who persecuted the first Christians until a light knocked him to the ground.
Acts says he worked as a tentmaker, and in his letters he says he worked night and day while he preached, so as not to be a burden. Now the argument.
In his letter to the Galatians, Paul tells how Peter came to Antioch and ate with Gentile Christians, then pulled back when some men came from James in Jerusalem.

teach.h: I WITHSTOOD HIM TO THE FACE.
teach.b: Paul writes: "I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed." The Church kept that letter in the Bible.
Both men ended up in Rome, and tradition says both died there under the emperor Nero. Peter, the story goes, was crucified, and asked to be crucified upside down.
Paul, a Roman citizen, was beheaded, which is why he holds a sword.

teach.h: I HAVE FINISHED MY COURSE, I HAVE KEPT THE FAITH.
teach.b: In the second letter to Timothy, Paul says: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith." Two pillars, the Church calls them. Different, sometimes at odds, holding up the same roof.

how: Catholics keep the solemnity of Saints Peter and Paul on 29 June; in Rome it's a city holiday, and the pope blesses the pallium, a woolen band, for archbishops appointed during the year.

o: Greek for rock, the name Jesus gave Simon
Greek for fisherman, Simon's old trade
Greek for keys, from Peter's statue

games.q: the two pillars — tap the pairs.

s: Paul writes in Galatians that he withstood Peter to the face at Antioch.
Paul holds a sword because he was a soldier
tradition says he was beheaded, as a Roman citizen; the sword recalls his death.
Acts says Paul worked as a tentmaker
and in his letters he says he worked so as not to be a burden.

games.q: you're Paul in Antioch. Peter has stopped eating with Gentile Christians since some men came from James. what do you do?
o: say nothing; he's the senior apostle.
confront him to his face, in front of everyone.
games.why: Paul writes, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. and the Church kept the letter in the Bible.

practice: Picture Rome: the basilica over Peter's grave, the pope, the parishes, the people on buses and the poor sleeping near the colonnade.
If you pray, you can pray for the pope and the people of Rome; if you don't, think of two people in your own life who don't always agree but hold something up together, and be grateful for both.

wordCard.voice: Petros. The Greek word for rock, the name Jesus gave Simon just before the keys of the kingdom. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: Petros, rock — the name Jesus gave to Simon.
